jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family, and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Capital campaigns, donor cultivation, major gifts, and every other form of fundraising are off your plate entirely
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Chief Development Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years leading high-stakes relationships in private or independent K-12 education, fundraising or major gifts, enterprise sales, client success, or private wealth management
2+ years working directly and regularly with ultra-high-net-worth or similarly high-expectation families, such as full-pay families at an elite private school, family-office clients, wealth-management clients, or major donors
Proven ownership of measurable enrollment, retention, advocacy, sales, or client outcomes, including resolving sensitive situations and holding firm standards when influential people push back
Polished executive communication, consultative judgment, and genuine conviction in Alpha's accelerated learning model, with the confidence to represent it to skeptical parents and public stakeholders
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area; authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship; and available for full-time on-site work, including 2 to 4 evening or weekend events per month

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Director of Partnerships & Advocacy based in the United States.

This is a senior leadership opportunity focused on advancing high-impact education policy initiatives at the national and state levels.

The role will initially lead a time-sensitive Federal Scholarship Tax Credit initiative, with significant responsibility for building political support across priority states.

You will develop multi-state strategies, cultivate senior government relationships, and build coalitions capable of influencing policy outcomes.

The position combines government relations, advocacy, strategic communications, campaign execution, and organizational leadership.

As priorities evolve, you will expand into additional federal and state initiatives, including opportunities connected to the 2028 presidential cycle.

You will work in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment where strategic judgment, political relationships, and rapid execution are essential.

The role offers the opportunity to shape both immediate policy outcomes and the infrastructure supporting future national education initiatives.

Accountabilities

Design and lead national and state-level strategies to build stakeholder and political support for Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) adoption across priority states.
Develop and manage state-specific advocacy plans in close collaboration with policymakers, coalition partners, and local stakeholders.
Monitor gubernatorial, legislative, and political developments in priority states and adapt strategies quickly as circumstances change.
Translate policy research, polling, and data into compelling state-specific messaging, factsheets, presentations, toolkits, and other advocacy materials.
Oversee targeted multi-channel digital communications campaigns designed to demonstrate the benefits of FSTC initiatives for families.
Present and communicate polling and public opinion research, including national and state-level findings, to relevant stakeholders.
Build and maintain senior-level relationships with center-left governors, gubernatorial candidates, senior staff, campaign teams, and executive-branch decision-makers.
Develop and sustain multi-stakeholder coalitions involving education advocates, charter and school-choice organizations, youth-serving groups, community organizations, and other aligned partners.
Coordinate coalition strategy and ensure partners remain aligned around shared policy and advocacy objectives.
Manage budgets across multiple organizational entities, ensuring resources are effectively allocated across lobbying, communications, polling, research, and coalition-building activities.
Direct external consultants and vendors while maintaining accountability for deliverables, timelines, and outcomes.
Report campaign progress and impact to senior leadership and contribute to fundraising efforts by demonstrating the effectiveness and reach of major initiatives.
As priorities expand, support engagement around the 2028 presidential cycle and identify and launch new mission-aligned state and federal initiatives.
Help build the systems, processes, partnerships, and organizational infrastructure needed to support a growing portfolio of initiatives.

Requirements

Significant knowledge of K–12 education policy, with experience or familiarity in areas such as school choice, charter schools, and education reform strongly preferred.
Demonstrated commitment to educational equity and expanding opportunities for underserved students and families.
Proven experience in political campaigns, government affairs, public policy, or advocacy, with a track record of successfully advancing complex legislative or executive-branch initiatives at the state or federal level.
Strong relationships with center-left governors, gubernatorial staff, presidential campaign alumni, executive-branch officials, or other influential political decision-makers are highly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build, manage, and align complex coalitions involving diverse political, policy, nonprofit, and community stakeholders.
Strong strategic communication skills, including the ability to turn complex policy issues into compelling narratives for policymakers, partners, media, and the public.
Experience overseeing digital advocacy campaigns, earned media, public engagement, polling, or related communications efforts.
Strong project and budget management capabilities, with experience managing multiple workstreams, contractors, consultants, and budgets simultaneously.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift quickly and execution timelines are demanding.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to build systems and structures while simultaneously delivering against immediate strategic objectives.
Strong judgment, relationship-building skills, political awareness, and ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Long-term strategic perspective and the ability to connect immediate campaign objectives with broader organizational capacity and future priorities.
Strong commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and expanding educational opportunity for low-income families and families of color.
Must be legally authorized to work for any employer in the United States; employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Ability and willingness to travel approximately 20% as required.

Competitive annual compensation of $160,000–$180,000, commensurate with experience.
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance.
Flexible Spending Account (FSA).

Floating holidays and paid national holidays.

gt.school is redefining what school should look like for high-potential students. Our 2 Hour Learning model compresses the academic day into focused, mastery-based sessions—freeing up time for students to pursue real challenges. Now, we’re ready to build out a physical model campus that adds the missing pieces: leadership experiences, peer competition, performance-driven culture, and the kind of community these students have been missing.

You’ll lead the design, validation, and public rollout of this model campus—with the goal of making it the prototype for a nationwide network. You'll also continue to build our virtual GT Anywhere program together with the team we already have in place. That means testing real-world programming, developing parent demand, building a culture that sticks, and crafting the playbooks to scale it all.

We need someone with founder-level energy and credibility. Someone who understands that the best ideas mean nothing without relentless execution. Someone who can turn a sharp point of view into a school parents can’t stop talking about—and students can’t wait to attend.

Designing and testing scalable programs that extend beyond academics—focusing on leadership, independence, and competition
Building and validating a physical model campus, including staffing models, space design, and operations
Developing parent-facing messaging, market strategies, and growth playbooks to fuel expansion
Defining, documenting, and scaling quality standards and cultural rituals across all future sites
Acting as the public face of the model—driving visibility through media, events, and partnerships

What You Won’t Be Doing

Stepping into a traditional school role with classrooms, teachers, and a full-day schedule
Catering to families who want gifted-lite programs with AP classes and minimal challenge
Managing incremental change within existing institutions—we're not "fixing" schools, we're replacing them
Chasing superficial engagement metrics—we care about hard outcomes and deep learning, not just activity
Building everything remotely—you'll have flexibility, but will spend ~1 week/month in Austin to ground your work in reality

Program Director Key Responsibilities

Design, validate, and scale a high-performance gifted school model—starting with a single prototype campus and expanding to a national network.

Built and scaled a high-impact venture from scratch (bonus if it involved physical operations or education). We are talking about at least 1M USD yearly revenue owned by you
Deep, personal understanding of gifted students—whether through family, professional experience, or lived reality
AI First mentality — Inclination to prioritize AI as the default solution for problem-solving, decision-making and work output generation at scale.

Based in the U.S., with ability to travel regularly to Austin (minimum 1 week/month)
Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

GT School is revolutionizing education with AI, expert coaching, and 50+ years of learning science. They blend cutting-edge tech with data-driven insights to unlock every student's full potential.

"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family, and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Capital campaigns, donor cultivation, major gifts, and every other form of fundraising are off your plate entirely
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Chief Development Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years leading high-stakes relationships in private or independent K-12 education, fundraising or major gifts, enterprise sales, client success, or private wealth management
2+ years working directly and regularly with ultra-high-net-worth or similarly high-expectation families, such as full-pay families at an elite private school, family-office clients, wealth-management clients, or major donors
Proven ownership of measurable enrollment, retention, advocacy, sales, or client outcomes, including resolving sensitive situations and holding firm standards when influential people push back
Polished executive communication, consultative judgment, and genuine conviction in Alpha's accelerated learning model, with the confidence to represent it to skeptical parents and public stakeholders
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area; authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship; and available for full-time on-site work, including 2 to 4 evening or weekend events per month

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role
